<reason>Both sides fought a genuinely sharp, narrowing debate. CON built the best available offensive frame: the motion's operative verb is "replace," and replacing worker-owned tips with house-owned service charges transfers a discretionary income stream from labor to management, which is why tipped workers themselves have organized against abolition (DC, Maine) and why the Meyer experiment failed. CON's "statute invented in the fourth speech" hit on PRO's answer was the strongest single counterpunch. But PRO won the two decisive comparisons. First, the textual one: the proposition says "tipping-based compensation" and "rather than rely on customer guilt," so a living wage funded by honest, printed prices with a residual voluntary gift satisfies the motion — and CON's own final ledger (print the charge, raise the floor, pool with the kitchen, "I have conceded all of it") is that world. CON's dilemma is clever, but it left CON defending only the optional upside above a floor it had already agreed to raise. Second, the normative one: PRO's variance-allocation frame (the business that sets prices and schedules should carry the risk, not the worker with the thinnest cushion) plus the neglected constituencies (lunch server, dead section, kitchen, harassment leverage) was never squarely answered; CON's reply that "the floor already exists in law" is undercut by CON's own concession that the floor should be raised, and CON's nurse-analogy answer ("no discretionary surplus at a bedside") conceded the general principle. PRO also turned CON's trust-the-owner objection back on CON's tip-pooling remedy. PRO's three clipped speeches are a real execution cost and keep the margin from being larger; CON's closing was the crisper piece of writing, but it crystallized a narrower ground than it needed.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>PRO's [B4.2]: CON's own remedy for the kitchen is tip pooling administered by the same owner CON says cannot be trusted with a service-charge dollar — "if owner discretion is fatal to my mechanism, it is fatal to CON's." Combined with harvesting CON's concessions (legible menu, raise the floor, share with the kitchen) to show CON had already built the PRO world, this collapsed CON's live route to the narrow question of the residual upside.</best_rebuttal>
